finding: A function that a test calls gets 0 % when its line starts several functions whose lcov records differ in count. The rule protects against IMPL-0112, because lcov cannot tell the functions of such a line apart. A story that changes such a line can therefore fail the gate wrongly, for example with a called function of complexity 6, which scores 42 at 0 %. Reproduction: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-matthiasdaues-Documents-datenschoenheit-agent-factory/89fd1670-49e4-4a59-97db-e1035150aa04/scratchpad/st0449-review/repro_typescript.sh <command> two-processes gives outer, outer.(anonymous) and later each 0 %, although tests call outer and later. Fix: read the V8 coverage files that NODE_V8_COVERAGE writes, which give each function its start offset and count, and pair by offset. Until then, the header could name the rule as a known limit, and the developer can split such a line.
why_this_severity: DEC-84 accepts a wrong failure, and the code of this repository rarely starts several functions on one line (no to fails_purpose). A story that changes such a line gets a failure that its tests cannot fix.
